views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Do not add new tariffs, raise the announced 10% List 4 rate, or expand entity-list/export-control measures before the September talks. Keep the Sept 1 List 4 date and the Huawei listing as leverage, but use the remaining weeks to reconvene the already-scheduled Washington round around three narrow asks: restore U.S. farm purchases, stop further competitive FX signaling, and restart the structural IP/enforcement text that stalled after May. Treat Sept 1 as a deadline that can be staged or paused if Beijing puts real purchases and text back on the table—not as an automatic ratchet.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is moderately elevated for the United States, not existential and not an opportunity. Combined Section 301 coverage is already ~$250B at 25%; the Aug 1 announcement of 10% on the remaining ~$300B (List 4) would land on clothes, toys, phones and other retail goods, which retailers and TD Securities warned would hit U.S. growth, inflation and low-income households more than prior industrial lists. China answered within days by suspending U.S. agricultural purchases and not ruling out tariffs on post-Aug 3 farm cargo—American Farm Bureau called that a "body blow" after soy exports had already collapsed (10.1 mt YTD vs 27.5 mt a year earlier; China farm imports $9.1B in 2018 vs $19.5B in 2017). The yuan break through 7 and the Aug 5 manipulator designation opened a currency channel that can offset U.S. tariff pressure while the 10-year yield fell to 1.71% (from 2.65% in February) and the 3m–10y inversion deepened to the worst since the financial crisis; the Fed had just cut (effective funds 2.13% in August). That is material GDP/political risk, especially in the farm belt, but it is not +0.5: List 4 is not yet in force, unemployment was still ~3.7%, and the manipulator label is largely IMF-referral symbolism. Action stays near zero because Washington already escalated twice in a week (List 4; currency designation). Piling on now would raise the odds China walks from the September round—the U.S.-China Business Council warned the new tariffs would drive Beijing from the table—and deepen the market/recession feedback already visible on Aug 5 (Dow −767, S&P −3%). Rolling back before China restores purchases or reopens structural text would reward the post-Osaka stall and the May backtracking on IP/enforcement. Negotiate, with existing measures held in place, is the stance that matches a mid-range threat.
key_factors: List 4 (10% on ~$300B, Sept 1) hits consumer goods and is not yet in force
China suspended U.S. farm purchases after calling List 4 a violation of the Osaka truce
Yuan break of 7 plus Treasury manipulator designation opens a currency offset and a second front
Markets: worst 2019 equity day, 10-year at 1.71%, deepest 3m–10y inversion since the financial crisis
September Washington talks remain on the calendar after a no-progress Shanghai round
Huawei stays on the Entity List; G20 'relief' is licenses only, still usable leverage
Domestic split: farm-belt and retailer pain vs bipartisan hawk support for toughness

sources_cited.excerpt: After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
Trade talks in Shanghai (through July 31). Little progress reported.
G20 Osaka: Trump and Xi agree to resume talks. Existing tariffs remain; no new tariffs for the time being.
Trump tweets negotiations are going too slowly and China is attempting to renegotiate; orders List 3 to 25% and preparation of tariffs on remaining ~$300B.
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List.
U.S. 10-year yield 1.71% on 2019-08-07, down 0.94pp (~35%) over the window.
Federal funds effective rate 2.13% on 2019-08-01, down from 2.40% in July after the first cut in over a decade.
List 4 hits clothes, toys, cell phones and retail items; 70% of U.S. shoes from China; USCBC warned escalation would drive China from the table.
Aug 5: S&P 500 -3%, Dow -767; 10-year to 1.72%; 3m yield 28bp above 10-year; recession still unlikely but probability higher.
China halted purchases of U.S. agricultural products and will not rule out tariffs on farm imports purchased after Aug. 3.
Treasury determined China is a currency manipulator and will engage the IMF; cites devaluation while holding large reserves.
TD: List 4 more consumer-oriented, larger impact on U.S. growth and inflation than prior hikes.
